We choose a safe value.\n    CFL = 0.05\n\n    # Create mesh and basis\n    print(f\"Creating mesh ({nx}x{ny}) and basis (N={polynomial_degree})...\")\n    mesh = Mesh(nx=nx, ny=ny, x_min=x_min, x_max=x_max, y_min=y_min, y_max=y_max, device=device)\n    basis = Basis(polynomial_degree=polynomial_degree, device=device)\n\n    # Create the solver\n    print(\"Initializing solver...\")\n    solver = DGSolver(mesh, basis, initial_conditions_func=initial_conditions_vortex)\n\n\n    output_dir = \"data\"\n    np.savez(\n        os.path.join(output_dir, \"init.npz\"), \n        q=solver.Q.numpy(), \n        x=solver.x.numpy(), \n        y=solver.y.numpy(),\n        vertices=mesh.vertices_host\n    )\n\n    # Run the simulation\n    print(f\"Starting simulation on device '{device}'...\")\n    print(f\"t_final = {t_final}, CFL = {CFL}\")\n    solver.solve(t_final=t_final, CFL=CFL, log_frequency=20)\n    print(\"Simulation finished.\")\n\n    # Save the solution\n    print(\"Saving solution to data/output.npz...\")\n    output_dir = \"data\"\n    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):\n        os.makedirs(output_dir)\n    \n    np.savez(\n        os.path.join(output_dir, \"output.npz\"), \n        q=solver.Q.numpy(), \n        x=solver.x.numpy(), \n        y=solver.y.numpy(),\n        vertices=mesh.vertices_host\n    )\n\n    print(\"Solution saved.\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"2D Discontinuous Galerkin Euler Solver with Nvidia Warp\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--poly_degree\", type=int, default=3, help=\"Polynomial degree for the basis functions.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--nx\", type=int, default=32, help=\"Number of elements in the x-direction.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--ny\", type=int, default=32, help=\"Number of elements in the y-direction.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--t_final\", type=float, default=20.0, help=\"Final simulation time.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--device\", type=str, default=\"cuda\", choices=[\"cuda\", \"cpu\"], help=\"Device to run the simulation on.\")\n    \n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    main(args)\n"

    "old_string": "from src.dg_solver.mesh import Mesh\nfrom src.dg_solver.basis import Basis\nfrom src.dg_solver.solver import DGSolver\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport os\nimport argparse\n\ndef initial_conditions_vortex(x, y):\n    \"\"\"\n    2D Isentropic Vortex problem.\n    This is a common test case for Euler solvers.\n    The solution is a vortex that advects diagonally across the domain.\n    \"\"\"\n    gamma = 1.4\n    beta = 5.0  # Vortex strength\n    r_sq = (x - 5.0)**2 + (y - 5.0)**2\n    \n    u_inf = 1.0\n    v_inf = 1.0\n    \n    du = -(beta / (2 * np.pi)) * np.exp(0.5 * (1 - r_sq)) * (y - 5.0)\n    dv = (beta / (2 * np.pi)) * np.exp(0.5 * (1 - r_sq)) * (x - 5.0)\n    \n    u = u_inf + du\n    v = v_inf + dv\n    \n    T_inf = 1.0\n    T = T_inf - ((gamma - 1) * beta**2 / (8 * gamma * np.pi**2)) * np.exp(1 - r_sq)\n    \n    rho = T**(1.0 / (gamma - 1))\n    p = rho**gamma\n    \n    return rho, u, v, p\n\ndef initial_conditions_uniform(x, y):\n    \"\"\"\n    Uniform flow.\n    \"\"\"\n    rho = 1.0\n    u = 1.0\n    v = 0.0\n    p = 1.0\n    return rho, u, v, p\n\n\ndef main(args):\n    # Simulation parameters\n    polynomial_degree = 4\n    nx = args.nx\n    ny = args.ny\n    t_final =20.0\n    device = args.device\n\n    # --- Domain ---\n    x_min, x_max = 0.0, 10.0\n    y_min, y_max = 0.0, 10.0\n    \n    # --- CFL condition ---\n    # dt = CFL * dx / ( |u| + c )\n    # For DG, CFL is restricted by ~1/(2N+1), where N is the polynomial degree.\n    # For N=3, CFL < 0.14. We choose a safe value.\n    CFL = 0.05\n\n    # Create mesh and basis\n    print(f\"Creating mesh ({nx}x{ny}) and basis (N={polynomial_degree})...\")\n    mesh = Mesh(nx=nx, ny=ny, x_min=x_min, x_max=x_max, y_min=y_min, y_max=y_max, device=device)\n    basis = Basis(polynomial_degree=polynomial_degree, device=device)\n\n    # Create the solver\n    print(\"Initializing solver...\")\n    solver = DGSolver(mesh, basis, initial_conditions_func=initial_conditions_vortex)\n\n\n    output_dir = \"data\"\n    np.savez(\n        os.path.join(output_dir, \"init.npz\"), \n        q=solver.Q.numpy(), \n        x=solver.x.numpy(), \n        y=solver.y.numpy(),\n        vertices=mesh.vertices_host\n    )\n\n    # Run the simulation\n    print(f\"Starting simulation on device '{device}'...\")\n    print(f\"t_final = {t_final}, CFL = {CFL}\")\n    solver.solve(t_final=t_final, CFL=CFL, log_frequency=20)\n    print(\"Simulation finished.\")\n\n    # Save the solution\n    print(\"Saving solution to data/output.npz...\")\n    output_dir = \"data\"\n    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):\n        os.makedirs(output_dir)\n    \n    np.savez(\n        os.path.join(output_dir, \"output.npz\"), \n        q=solver.Q.numpy(), \n        x=solver.x.numpy(), \n        y=solver.y.numpy(),\n        vertices=mesh.vertices_host\n    )\n\n    print(\"Solution saved.\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"2D Discontinuous Galerkin Euler Solver with Nvidia Warp\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--poly_degree\", type=int, default=3, help=\"Polynomial degree for the basis functions.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--nx\", type=int, default=32, help=\"Number of elements in the x-direction.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--ny\", type=int, default=32, help=\"Number of elements in the y-direction.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--t_final\", type=float, default=20.0, help=\"Final simulation time.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--device\", type=str, default=\"cuda\", choices=[\"cuda\", \"cpu\"], help=\"Device to run the simulation on.\")\n    \n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    main(args)\n"
  }

vertices are on host, so we use the host array\n            v = self.mesh.vertices_host[i, :, :] \n            dx_dr = dNd_r_center @ v[:, 0]\n            dx_ds = dNd_s_center @ v[:, 0]\n            dy_dr = dNd_r_center @ v[:, 1]\n            dy_ds = dNd_s_center @ v[:, 1]\n            J = dx_dr * dy_ds - dx_ds * dy_dr\n\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 0] = dx_dr\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 1] = dx_ds\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 2] = dy_dr\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 3] = dy_ds\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 4] = J\n            \n            #     "old_string": "from .mesh import Mesh\nfrom .basis import Basis\nfrom . import equations as eq\nfrom . import warp_kernels as wk\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport warp as wp\nimport os\n\nclass DGSolver:\n    def __init__(self, mesh: Mesh, basis: Basis, initial_conditions_func):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initializes the Discontinuous Galerkin solver.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.mesh = mesh\n        self.basis = basis\n        self.device = mesh.device\n        \n        # --- Host-side data (for setup) ---\n        self.geo_factors_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, 5), dtype=np.float32) # dx_dr, dx_ds, dy_dr, dy_ds, J\n        self.face_geo_factors_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, 4, 3), dtype=np.float32) # nx, ny, J_face\n        self.x_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, basis.Np), dtype=np.float32)\n        self.y_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, basis.Np), dtype=np.float32)\n        \n        self._calculate_geometric_factors()\n        self._map_nodes_to_physical_space()\n\n        # --- Device-side data (for computation) ---\n        self.geo_factors = wp.array(self.geo_factors_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n        self.face_geo_factors = wp.array(self.face_geo_factors_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n        self.x = wp.array(self.x_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n        self.y = wp.array(self.y_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n\n        # Inverse of Mass Matrix (diagonal)\n        weights_2d = np.kron(self.basis.weights_1d.numpy(), self.basis.weights_1d.numpy())\n        M_inv_diag_host = 1.0 / weights_2d\n        self.M_inv_diag = wp.array(M_inv_diag_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n\n        # Solution field\n        Q_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, basis.Np, 4), dtype=np.float32)\n        self._set_initial_conditions(Q_host, initial_conditions_func)\n        self.Q = wp.array(Q_host, dtype=wp.vec4, device=self.device)\n        self.Q_stage1 = wp.zeros_like(self.Q)\n        self.Q_stage2 = wp.zeros_like(self.Q)\n        self.Q_rk = self.Q # Input for the RHS computation\n        self.rhs = wp.zeros_like(self.Q)\n\n        self.max_wave_speed = wp.zeros(1, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n\n\n    def _calculate_geometric_factors(self):\n        \"\"\"\n        Calculates geometric factors for affine quadrilateral elements.\n        The transformation is x(r,s) = sum(N_i(r,s) * x_i), where N_i are bilinear shape functions.\n        For affine elements, the derivatives (and thus the Jacobian) are constant.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Derivatives of bilinear shape functions at the center (r=0, s=0)\n        dNd_r_center = 0.25 * np.array([-1, 1, 1, -1])\n        dNd_s_center = 0.25 * np.array([-1, -1, 1, 1])\n        \n        for i in range(self.mesh.num_elements):\n            # vertices are on host, so we use the host array\n            v = self.mesh.vertices_host[i, :, :] \n            dx_dr = dNd_r_center @ v[:, 0]\n            dx_ds = dNd_s_center @ v[:, 0]\n            dy_dr = dNd_r_center @ v[:, 1]\n            dy_ds = dNd_s_center @ v[:, 1]\n            J = dx_dr * dy_ds - dx_ds * dy_dr\n\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 0] = dx_dr\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 1] = dx_ds\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 2] = dy_dr\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 3] = dy_ds\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 4] = J\n            \n            # --- Face geometric factors ---\n            # Face 0 (bottom): s=-1, tangent (dx/dr, dy/dr)\n            nx, ny = dy_dr, -dx_dr\n            J_face = np.sqrt(nx**2 + ny**2)\n            self.face_geo_factors_host[i, 0, :] = [nx/J_face, ny/J_face, J_face]\n\n            # Face 1 (right): r=1, tangent (dx/ds, dy/ds)\n            nx, ny = dy_ds, -dx_ds\n            J_face = np.sqrt(nx**2 + ny**2)\n            self.face_geo_factors_host[i, 1, :] = [nx/J_face, ny/J_face, J_face]\n            \n            # Face 2 (top): s=1, tangent (dx/dr, dy/dr)\n            nx, ny = -dy_dr, dx_dr # Normal points outwards\n            J_face = np.sqrt(nx**2 + ny**2)\n            self.face_geo_factors_host[i, 2, :] = [nx/J_face, ny/J_face, J_face]\n\n            # Face 3 (left): r=-1, tangent (dx/ds, dy/ds)\n            nx, ny = -dy_ds, dx_ds # Normal points outwards\n            J_face = np.sqrt(nx**2 + ny**2)\n            self.face_geo_factors_host[i, 3, :] = [nx/J_face, ny/J_face, J_face]\n\n\n    def _map_nodes_to_physical_space(self):\n        \"\"\" Maps nodal points from the reference to the physical element. \"\"\"\n        r = self.basis.nodes_2d.numpy()[:, 0]; s = self.basis.nodes_2d.numpy()[:, 1]\n        N1 = 0.25*(1-r)*(1-s); N2 = 0.25*(1+r)*(1-s); N3 = 0.25*(1+r)*(1+s); N4 = 0.25*(1-r)*(1+s)\n        N = np.vstack([N1, N2, N3, N4])\n        for i in range(self.mesh.num_elements):\n            v = self.mesh.vertices_host[i, :, :]\n            self.x_host[i, :] = N.T @ v[:, 0]\n            self.y_host[i, :] = N.T @ v[:, 1]\n\n    def _set_initial_conditions(self, Q_host, func):\n        for i in range(self.mesh.num_elements):\n            for j in range(self.basis.Np):\n                rho, u, v, p = func(self.x_host[i, j], self.y_host[i, j])\n                Q_host[i, j, :] = eq.primitive_to_conservative([rho, u, v, p])\n\n    def _compute_rhs(self):\n        \"\"\" Computes the right-hand side of the ODE using Warp kernels. \"\"\"\n        self.rhs.zero_()\n        \n        # --- Volume Integral ---\n        wp.launch(\n            kernel=wk.compute_volume_term,\n            dim=(self.mesh.num_elements, self.basis.Np),\n            inputs=[\n                self.Q_rk,\n                self.rhs,\n                self.basis.Dr,\n                self.basis.Ds,\n                self.mesh.rx,\n                self.mesh.sy,\n                self.basis.Np\n            ],\n            device=self.device\n        )\n        \n        # --- Surface Integral ---\n        wp.launch(\n            kernel=wk.compute_surface_term,\n            dim=self.mesh.num_elements,  # Nur 1 Thread pro Element (Kernel loopt über Faces)\n            inputs=[\n                self.Q_rk,\n                self.rhs,\n                self.mesh.connectivity,\n                self.basis.face_nodes,\n                self.basis.LIFT,\n                self.mesh.Js_x,\n                self.mesh.Js_y,\n                self.mesh.J,\n                self.basis.Nfp\n            ],\n            device=self.device\n        )\n\n    def solve(self, t_final, CFL, log_frequency=10):\n        \"\"\" The main time-stepping loop. \"\"\"\n        t = 0.0\n        step = 0\n        \n        # --- Debugging: Directory to save step-by-step results ---\n        output_steps_dir = \"data/steps\"\n        if not os.path.exists(output_steps_dir):\n            os.makedirs(output_steps_dir)\n        \n        use_stream = self.device == \"cuda\"\n        if use_stream:\n            stream = wp.Stream(device=self.device)\n\n        while t < t_final:\n            \n            # --- Adaptive dt calculation ---\n            self.max_wave_speed.zero_()\n            wp.launch(\n                kernel=wk.compute_max_wave_speed,\n                dim=(self.mesh.num_elements, self.basis.Np),\n                inputs=[self.Q, self.max_wave_speed],\n                device=self.device\n            )\n            max_speed = self.max_wave_speed.numpy()[0]\n            print(f\"Max speed: {max_speed:.4e}\")\n            \n            # Ensure max_speed is not zero to avoid division by zero\n            # Also, handle the case where the simulation might start with zero velocity\n            if max_speed < 1.0e-6:\n                max_speed = 1.0 \n\n            # Smallest distance between any two nodes in the mesh (characteristic length)\n            # A simpler but less robust way is to use dx = mesh.lx / mesh.nx\n            dx = self.mesh.dx \n            dt = CFL * dx / max_speed\n            print(f\"Calculated dt: {dt:.4e}\")\n\n            # --- End of adaptive dt calculation ---\n\n            if use_stream:\n                with stream:\n                    # Standard SSP-RK3 scheme\n                    self.Q_rk = self.Q\n                    self._compute_rhs()\n                    wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_1, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q_stage1], device=self.device)\n                    \n                    self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage1\n                    self._compute_rhs()\n                    wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_2, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage1, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q_stage2], device=self.device)\n\n                    self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage2\n                    self._compute_rhs()\n                    wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_3, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage2, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q], device=self.device)\n                \n                stream.synchronize()\n            else: # Synchronous execution for CPU\n                # 1st stage\n                self.Q_rk = self.Q\n                self._compute_rhs()\n                wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_1, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q_stage1], device=self.device)\n                \n                # 2nd stage\n                self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage1\n                self._compute_rhs()\n                wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_2, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage1, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q_stage2], device=self.device)\n\n                # 3rd stage\n                self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage2\n                self._compute_rhs()\n                wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_3, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage2, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q], device=self.device)\n\n                # For CPU, a manual synchronize is good practice to ensure completion\n                wp.synchronize()\n\n\n            t += dt\n            step += 1\n\n            # --- Debugging: Check for NaNs and save step data ---\n            q_np = self.Q.numpy()\n            if np.isnan(q_np).any():\n                print(f\"!!! Simulation became unstable with NaN values at step {step} (t={t:.4f}).\")\n                print(f\"!!! The last valid data was saved at step {step-1}.\")\n                break\n            \n            # Save step data\n            step_filename = os.path.join(output_steps_dir, f\"step_{step:04d}.npz\")\n            np.savez(step_filename, q=q_np, x=self.x.numpy(), y=self.y.numpy(), vertices=self.mesh.vertices_host)\n\n            if step % log_frequency == 0:\n              print(f\"Step: {step}, t = {t:.4f} / {t_final}, dt = {dt:.3e}\")\n"
  }

Optimierung: 0.5 * (rho_u^2 + rho_v^2) / rho ist numerisch stabiler \n    # als 0.5 * rho * (u^2 + v^2), da u=rho_u/rho -> u^2 = rho_u^2/rho^2\n    # Das spart eine Division und ist bei kleinem rho genauer.\n    kinetic_energy = 0.5 * (rho_u**2 + rho_v**2) / rho\n    p_val = (gamma - 1) * (E - kinetic_energy)\n    \n    return np.maximum(p_val, 1e-12)\n\ndef euler_fluxes(Q):\n    \"\"\"\n    Computes both F and G at once to save unpack operations/pressure calcs.\n    Returns F, G\n    \"\"\"\n    rho, rho_u, rho_v, E = Q\n    rho = np.maximum(rho, 1e-12)\n    p = pressure(Q)\n    \n    # Inverse density\n    inv_rho = 1.0 / rho\n    u = rho_u * inv_rho\n    v = rho_v * inv_rho\n    \n    # Flux F (x-dir)\n    f1 = rho_u\n    f2 = rho_u * u + p\n    f3 = rho_u * v     # rho_v * u ist das gleiche wie rho_u * v\n    f4 = (E + p) * u\n    \n    # Flux G (y-dir)\n    g1 = rho_v\n    g2 = rho_v * u     # rho_u * v\n    g3 = rho_v * v + p\n    g4 = (E + p) * v\n    \n    F = np.array([f1, f2, f3, f4])\n    G = np.array([g1, g2, g3, g4])\n    return F, G\n\ndef get_max_eigenvalue(Q, normal_vector):\n    rho = Q[0]\n    # Vermeide Division durch fast-Null\n    rho = np.maximum(rho, 1e-12)\n    p = pressure(Q)\n    \n    # Sound speed\n    c = np.sqrt(gamma * p / rho)\n    \n    nx, ny = normal_vector\n    # Velocity projected on normal\n    # u_n = (rho_u * nx + rho_v * ny) / rho\n    u_n = (Q[1] * nx + Q[2] * ny) / rho\n    \n    return np.abs(u_n) + c\n\ndef lax_friedrichs_flux(q_l, q_r, normal_vector):\n    \"\"\"\n    Computes the Lax-Friedrichs numerical flux projected on the normal.\n    \"\"\"\n    nx, ny = normal_vector\n    \n    # Compute fluxes\n    # Wir nutzen hier die kombinierte Funktion, um Rechenzeit zu sparen\n    F_l, G_l = euler_fluxes(q_l)\n    F_r, G_r = euler_fluxes(q_r)\n    \n    # Projected fluxes (Flux dot Normal)\n    flux_n_l = F_l * nx + G_l * ny\n    flux_n_r = F_r * nx + G_r * ny\n    \n    # Max eigenvalue (wave speed)\n    lambda_l = get_max_eigenvalue(q_l, normal_vector)\n    lambda_r = get_max_eigenvalue(q_r, normal_vector)\n    \n    # Global max wave speed at the interface\n    alpha = np.maximum(lambda_l, lambda_r)\n    \n    # Broadcasting Safety: alpha auf (1, N) bringen falls q (4, N) ist\n    # Das verhindert Fehler, falls die Dimensionen mal drehen\n    if alpha.ndim == 1:\n        alpha_b = alpha[None, :] \n    else:\n        alpha_b = alpha\n\n    # Numerical Flux Formula\n    # F_num = 0.5 * (F_L + F_R) - 0.5 * alpha * (Q_R - Q_L)\n    flux = 0.5 * (flux_n_l + flux_n_r) - 0.5 * alpha_b * (q_r - q_l)\n    \n    return flux\n\ndef primitive_to_conservative(prim):\n    \"\"\"\n    Converts primitive variables [rho, u, v, p] to conservative variables [rho, rho*u, rho*v, E].\n    \"\"\"\n    rho, u, v, p = prim\n    rho_u = rho * u\n    rho_v = rho * v\n    kinetic_energy = 0.5 * rho * (u**2 + v**2)\n    E = p / (gamma - 1) + kinetic_energy\n    return np.array([rho, rho_u, rho_v, E])\n\ndef conservative_to_primitive(Q):\n    \"\"\"\n    Converts conservative variables [rho, rho*u, rho*v, E] back to primitive [rho, u, v, p].\n    Used for visualization.\n    \"\"\"\n    rho, rho_u, rho_v, E = Q\n    \n    # Avoid division by zero\n    rho_safe = np.maximum(rho, 1e-12)\n    \n    u = rho_u / rho_safe\n    v = rho_v / rho_safe\n    p_val = pressure(Q) # Nutzt die bereits vorhandene pressure-Funktion\n    \n    return np.array([rho, u, v, p_val])"
  }
}

Chain rule: dF/dx = dF/dr * dr/dx  (da dr/dy = 0 etc. bei Rechtecken)\n    div_F = dF_dr * dr_dx + dG_ds * ds_dy\n    \n    # RHS update (Strong Form: rhs = -div F)\n    # Wir benutzen atomic_sub, falls wir diesen Kernel mehrmals aufrufen würden, \n    # aber hier reicht direktes Zuweisen, wenn wir RHS vorher nullen.\n    rhs[e, i] = -div_F \n\n\n@wp.kernel\ndef compute_surface_term(\n    q: wp.array(dtype=wp.vec4, ndim=2),        # State\n    rhs: wp.array(dtype=wp.vec4, ndim=2),      # Bottom (y=-1)\n            nx = 0.0; ny = -1.0; surf_J = surf_J_y\n        elif face_idx == 1: # Right (x=+1)\n            nx = 1.0; ny = 0.0; surf_J = surf_J_x\n        elif face_idx == 2: # Top (y=+1)\n            nx = 0.0; ny = 1.0; surf_J = surf_J_y\n        elif face_idx == 3: # Left (x=-1)\n            nx = -1.0; ny = 0.0; surf_J = surf_J_x\n\n        # Get Neighbor Info\n        # Connectivity speichert hier [neighbor_id, neighbor_face_index]\n        # Vereinfachung: Wir nehmen an, connectivity ist (NumElems, 4) mit NeighborIDs\n        # Zustand laden\n    val = q[e, i]\n    rho = wp.max(val[0], rho_floor)\n    \n    # Primitive Variablen\n    u = val[1] / rho\n    v = val[2] / rho\n    p = pressure(val)\n    \n    # Schallgeschwindigkeit c\n    c = wp.sqrt(gamma * p / rho)\n    \n    # Q_n (Startzustand)\n    q_1: wp.array(dtype=wp.vec4, ndim=2),    # Q(1) aus Stage 1\n    rhs: wp.array(dtype=wp.vec4, ndim=2),    # RHS(Q(1))\n    dt: wp.float32,\n    q_out: wp.array(dtype=wp.vec4, ndim=2)   # Ziel für Q(2)\n):\n    \"\"\"\n    Stage 2: Q(2) = 3/4 * Q_n + 1/4 * (Q(1) + dt * RHS(Q(1)))\n    \"\"\"\n    e, i = wp.tid()\n    # 0.75 * Q_n + 0.25 * (Q_1 + dt * RHS)\n    q_out[e, i] = 0.75 * q[e, i] + 0.25 * (q_1[e, i] + dt * rhs[e, i])\n\n@wp.kernel\ndef rk_stage_3(\n    q: wp.array(dtype=wp.vec4, ndim=2),      # Q_n\n    q_2: wp.array(dtype=wp.vec4, ndim=2),    # Q(2) aus Stage 2\n    rhs: wp.array(dtype=wp.vec4, ndim=2),    # RHS(Q(2))\n    dt: wp.float32,\n    q_out: wp.array(dtype=wp.vec4, ndim=2)   # Ziel für Q(n+1) (überschreibt oft self.Q)\n    ):\n    \"\"\"\n    Stage 3: Q(n+1) = 1/3 * Q_n + 2/3 * (Q(2) + dt * RHS(Q(2)))\n    \"\"\"\n    e, i = wp.tid()\n    # 1/3 * Q_n + 2/3 * (Q_2 + dt * RHS)\n    q_out[e, i] = (1.0/3.0) * q[e, i] + (2.0/3.0) * (q_2[e, i] + dt* rhs[e, i])"

🧑‍💻 ## USER

What is the difference between validation and verification in cfd simulation?

---

✨ ## MODEL

In the context of Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), the difference is often summarized by two questions:

1.  **Verification (Solving the equations *right*):**
    *   **Focus:** Mathematics and Software Quality.
    *   **Goal:** To demonstrate that the code is free of bugs and that the numerical algorithm (e.g., Discontinuous Galerkin) accurately solves the chosen mathematical model (e.g., Euler equations).
    *   **Methods:** Grid convergence studies (does error drop as mesh is refined?), code reviews, and comparison against **analytical solutions**.
    *   **Context for your project:** The **Isentropic Vortex** test case currently in `run_simulation.py` is a **Verification** case. It compares your numerical result against an exact mathematical solution to prove the solver works.

2.  **Validation (Solving the *right* equations):**
    *   **Focus:** Physics and Reality.
    *   **Goal:** To demonstrate that the mathematical model accurately represents the real-world physical phenomenon.
    *   **Methods:** Comparing simulation results against **experimental data** (wind tunnel) or real-world observations.
    *   **Context for your project:** Since your solver uses **Euler equations** (inviscid, no friction), it would fail **Validation** for calculating skin-friction drag on a car, even if the code is perfectly verified, because the physics model ignores viscosity.

**Summary:**
*   **Verification:** "Is the code bug-free and numerically correct?"
*   **Validation:** "Does the simulation match reality?"

I'll start with **Step 1: Update `src/kernels/warp_kernels.py`**.

Current:
```python
    # Chain rule: dF/dx = dF/dr * dr/dx  (da dr/dy = 0 etc. bei Rechtecken)
    div_F = dF_dr * dr_dx + dG_ds * ds_dy
```

New:
```python
    # Chain rule for F(x,y) -> F(r,s)
    # dF/dx = dF/dr * dr/dx + dF/ds * ds/dx
    # dF/dy = dF/dr * dr/dy + dF/ds * ds/dy
    
    # Divergence div(F) = dF_x/dx + dF_y/dy
    # Here F_vec = (F, G).  dF/dx + dG/dy
    
    # dF/dx = (dF/dr * dr_dx + dF/ds * ds_dx)
    # dG/dy = (dG/dr * dr_dy + dG/ds * ds_dy)
```

Wait, `compute_volume_term` computes `dF/dr` and `dG/ds`?
No, it accumulates:
```python
        dF_dr += F_val * Dr[i, j]
        dG_ds += G_val * Ds[i, j]
```
Actually, `Dr` computes derivative with respect to `r`.
For general curvilinear coordinates, we need:
$\frac{\partial \mathbf{F}}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial \mathbf{F}}{\partial r} \frac{\partial r}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial \mathbf{F}}{\partial s} \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}$
$\frac{\partial \mathbf{G}}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial \mathbf{G}}{\partial r} \frac{\partial r}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial \mathbf{G}}{\partial s} \frac{\partial s}{\partial y}$

So I need to compute `dF_dr`, `dF_ds`, `dG_dr`, `dG_ds`.
Current code only computes `dF_dr` and `dG_ds`.
I need to add `dF_ds` and `dG_dr`.

Modified Kernel Plan:
inputs: `rx`, `ry`, `sx`, `sy` (instead of just `rx`, `sy`).

```python
@wp.kernel
def compute_volume_term(
    # ...
    rx: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32, ndim=1),
    ry: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32, ndim=1), # NEW
    sx: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32, ndim=1), # NEW
    sy: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32, ndim=1),
    # ...
):
    # ...
    dF_dr = wp.vec4(0.0)
    dF_ds = wp.vec4(0.0) # NEW
    dG_dr = wp.vec4(0.0) # NEW
    dG_ds = wp.vec4(0.0)

    for j in range(Np):
        # ...
        dF_dr += F_val * Dr[i, j]
        dF_ds += F_val * Ds[i, j] # NEW
        
        dG_dr += G_val * Dr[i, j] # NEW
        dG_ds += G_val * Ds[i, j]

    # div F = dF/dx + dG/dy
    dF_dx = dF_dr * rx[e] + dF_ds * sx[e]
    dG_dy = dG_dr * ry[e] + dG_ds * sy[e]
    
    rhs[e, i] = -(dF_dx + dG_dy)
```

    "old_string": "from src.geometry.mesh import Mesh\nfrom .basis import Basis\nfrom src.physics import equations as eq\nfrom src.kernels import warp_kernels as wk\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport warp as wp\nimport os\n\nclass DGSolver:\n    def __init__(self, mesh: Mesh, basis: Basis, initial_conditions_func):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initializes the Discontinuous Galerkin solver.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.mesh = mesh\n        self.basis = basis\n        self.device = mesh.device\n        \n        # --- Host-side data (for setup) ---\n        self.geo_factors_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, 5), dtype=np.float32) # dx_dr, dx_ds, dy_dr, dy_ds, J\n        self.face_geo_factors_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, 4, 3), dtype=np.float32) # nx, ny, J_face\n        self.x_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, basis.Np), dtype=np.float32)\n        self.y_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, basis.Np), dtype=np.float32)\n        \n        self._calculate_geometric_factors()\n        self._map_nodes_to_physical_space()\n\n        # --- Device-side data (for computation) ---\n        self.geo_factors = wp.array(self.geo_factors_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n        self.face_geo_factors = wp.array(self.face_geo_factors_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n        self.x = wp.array(self.x_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n        self.y = wp.array(self.y_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n\n        # Inverse of Mass Matrix (diagonal)\n        weights_2d = np.kron(self.basis.weights_1d.numpy(), self.basis.weights_1d.numpy())\n        M_inv_diag_host = 1.0 / weights_2d\n        self.M_inv_diag = wp.array(M_inv_diag_host, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n\n        # Solution field\n        Q_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, basis.Np, 4), dtype=np.float32)\n        self._set_initial_conditions(Q_host, initial_conditions_func)\n        self.Q = wp.array(Q_host, dtype=wp.vec4, device=self.device)\n        self.Q_stage1 = wp.zeros_like(self.Q)\n        self.Q_stage2 = wp.zeros_like(self.Q)\n        self.Q_rk = self.Q # Input for the RHS computation\n        self.rhs = wp.zeros_like(self.Q)\n\n        self.max_wave_speed = wp.zeros(1, dtype=wp.float32, device=self.device)\n\n\n    def _calculate_geometric_factors(self):\n        \"\"\"\n        Calculates geometric factors for affine quadrilateral elements.\n        The transformation is x(r,s) = sum(N_i(r,s) * x_i), where N_i are bilinear shape functions.\n        For affine elements, the derivatives (and thus the Jacobian) are constant.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Derivatives of bilinear shape functions at the center (r=0, s=0)\n        dNd_r_center = 0.25 * np.array([-1, 1, 1, -1])\n        dNd_s_center = 0.25 * np.array([-1, -1, 1, 1])\n        \n        for i in range(self.mesh.num_elements):\n            # vertices are on host, so we use the host array\n            v = self.mesh.vertices_host[i, :, :] \n            dx_dr = dNd_r_center @ v[:, 0]\n            dx_ds = dNd_s_center @ v[:, 0]\n            dy_dr = dNd_r_center @ v[:, 1]\n            dy_ds = dNd_s_center @ v[:, 1]\n            J = dx_dr * dy_ds - dx_ds * dy_dr\n\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 0] = dx_dr\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 1] = dx_ds\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 2] = dy_dr\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 3] = dy_ds\n            self.geo_factors_host[i, 4] = J\n            \n            # --- Face geometric factors ---\n            # Face 0 (bottom): s=-1, tangent (dx/dr, dy/dr)\n            nx, ny = dy_dr, -dx_dr\n            J_face = np.sqrt(nx**2 + ny**2)\n            self.face_geo_factors_host[i, 0, :] = [nx/J_face, ny/J_face, J_face]\n\n            # Face 1 (right): r=1, tangent (dx/ds, dy/ds)\n            nx, ny = dy_ds, -dx_ds\n            J_face = np.sqrt(nx**2 + ny**2)\n            self.face_geo_factors_host[i, 1, :] = [nx/J_face, ny/J_face, J_face]\n            \n            # Face 2 (top): s=1, tangent (dx/dr, dy/dr)\n            nx, ny = -dy_dr, dx_dr # Normal points outwards\n            J_face = np.sqrt(nx**2 + ny**2)\n            self.face_geo_factors_host[i, 2, :] = [nx/J_face, ny/J_face, J_face]\n\n            # Face 3 (left): r=-1, tangent (dx/ds, dy/ds)\n            nx, ny = -dy_ds, dx_ds # Normal points outwards\n            J_face = np.sqrt(nx**2 + ny**2)\n            self.face_geo_factors_host[i, 3, :] = [nx/J_face, ny/J_face, J_face]\n\n\n    def _map_nodes_to_physical_space(self):\n        \"\"\" Maps nodal points from the reference to the physical element. \"\"\"\n        r = self.basis.nodes_2d.numpy()[:, 0]; s = self.basis.nodes_2d.numpy()[:, 1]\n        N1 = 0.25*(1-r)*(1-s); N2 = 0.25*(1+r)*(1-s); N3 = 0.25*(1+r)*(1+s); N4 = 0.25*(1-r)*(1+s)\n        N = np.vstack([N1, N2, N3, N4])\n        for i in range(self.mesh.num_elements):\n            v = self.mesh.vertices_host[i, :, :]\n            self.x_host[i, :] = N.T @ v[:, 0]\n            self.y_host[i, :] = N.T @ v[:, 1]\n\n    def _set_initial_conditions(self, Q_host, func):\n        for i in range(self.mesh.num_elements):\n            for j in range(self.basis.Np):\n                rho, u, v, p = func(self.x_host[i, j], self.y_host[i, j])\n                Q_host[i, j, :] = eq.primitive_to_conservative([rho, u, v, p])\n\n    def _compute_rhs(self):\n        \"\"\" Computes the right-hand side of the ODE using Warp kernels. \"\"\"\n        self.rhs.zero_()\n        \n        # --- Volume Integral ---\n        wp.launch(\n            kernel=wk.compute_volume_term,\n            dim=(self.mesh.num_elements, self.basis.Np),\n            inputs=[\n                self.Q_rk,\n                self.rhs,\n                self.basis.Dr,\n                self.basis.Ds,\n                self.mesh.rx,\n                self.mesh.sy,\n                self.basis.Np\n            ],\n            device=self.device\n        )\n        \n        # --- Surface Integral ---\n        wp.launch(\n            kernel=wk.compute_surface_term,\n            dim=self.mesh.num_elements,  # Nur 1 Thread pro Element (Kernel loopt über Faces)\n            inputs=[\n                self.Q_rk,\n                self.rhs,\n                self.mesh.connectivity,\n                self.basis.face_nodes,\n                self.basis.LIFT,\n                self.mesh.Js_x,\n                self.mesh.Js_y,\n                self.mesh.J,\n                self.basis.Nfp\n            ],\n            device=self.device\n        )\n\n    def solve(self, t_final, CFL, log_frequency=10):\n        \"\"\" The main time-stepping loop. \"\"\"\n        t = 0.0\n        step = 0\n        \n        # --- Debugging: Directory to save step-by-step results ---\n        output_steps_dir = \"data/steps\"\n        if not os.path.exists(output_steps_dir):\n            os.makedirs(output_steps_dir)\n        \n        use_stream = self.device == \"cuda\"\n        if use_stream:\n            stream = wp.Stream(device=self.device)\n\n        while t < t_final:\n            \n            # --- Adaptive dt calculation ---\n            self.max_wave_speed.zero_()\n            wp.launch(\n                kernel=wk.compute_max_wave_speed,\n                dim=(self.mesh.num_elements, self.basis.Np),\n                inputs=[self.Q, self.max_wave_speed],\n                device=self.device\n            )\n            max_speed = self.max_wave_speed.numpy()[0]\n            print(f\"Max speed: {max_speed:.4e}\")\n            \n            # Ensure max_speed is not zero to avoid division by zero\n            # Also, handle the case where the simulation might start with zero velocity\n            if max_speed < 1.0e-6:\n                max_speed = 1.0 \n\n            # Smallest distance between any two nodes in the mesh (characteristic length)\n            # A simpler but less robust way is to use dx = mesh.lx / mesh.nx\n            dx = self.mesh.dx \n            dt = CFL * dx / max_speed\n            print(f\"Calculated dt: {dt:.4e}\")\n\n            # --- End of adaptive dt calculation ---\n\n            if use_stream:\n                with stream:\n                    # Standard SSP-RK3 scheme\n                    self.Q_rk = self.Q\n                    self._compute_rhs()\n                    wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_1, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q_stage1], device=self.device)\n                    \n                    self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage1\n                    self._compute_rhs()\n                    wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_2, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage1, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q_stage2], device=self.device)\n\n                    self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage2\n                    self._compute_rhs()\n                    wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_3, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage2, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q], device=self.device)\n                \n                stream.synchronize()\n            else: # {
  "id": "read_file-1766216954874-553b5b2e5068c8",
  "name": "read_file",
  "response": {
    "output": "from src.geometry.mesh import Mesh\nfrom src.core.basis import Basis\nfrom src.core.solver import DGSolver\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport os\nimport argparse\n\ndef initial_conditions_vortex(x, y):\n    \"\"\"\n    2D Isentropic Vortex problem.\n    This is a common test case for Euler solvers.\n    The solution is a vortex that advects diagonally across the domain.\n    \"\"\"\n    gamma = 1.4\n    beta = 5.0  # Vortex strength\n    r_sq = (x - 5.0)**2 + (y - 5.0)**2\n    \n    u_inf = 1.0\n    v_inf = 1.0\n    \n    du = -(beta / (2 * np.pi)) * np.exp(0.5 * (1 - r_sq)) * (y - 5.0)\n    dv = (beta / (2 * np.pi)) * np.exp(0.5 * (1 - r_sq)) * (x - 5.0)\n    \n    u = u_inf + du\n    v = v_inf + dv\n    \n    T_inf = 1.0\n    T = T_inf - ((gamma - 1) * beta**2 / (8 * gamma * np.pi**2)) * np.exp(1 - r_sq)\n    \n    rho = T**(1.0 / (gamma - 1))\n    p = rho**gamma\n    \n    return rho, u, v, p\n\ndef initial_conditions_uniform(x, y):\n    \"\"\"\n    Uniform flow.\n    \"\"\"\n    rho = 1.0\n    u = 1.0\n    v = 0.0\n    p = 1.0\n    return rho, u, v, p\n\n\ndef main(args):\n    # Simulation parameters\n    polynomial_degree = 4\n    nx = args.nx\n    ny = args.ny\n    t_final =20.0\n    device = args.device\n\n    # --- Domain ---\n    x_min, x_max = 0.0, 10.0\n    y_min, y_max = 0.0, 10.0\n    \n    # --- CFL condition ---\n    # dt = CFL * dx / ( |u| + c )\n    # For DG, CFL is restricted by ~1/(2N+1), where N is the polynomial degree.\n    # For N=3, CFL < 0.14. We choose a safe value.\n    CFL = 0.05\n\n    # Create mesh and basis\n    print(f\"Creating mesh ({nx}x{ny}) and basis (N={polynomial_degree})...\")\n    mesh = Mesh(nx=nx, ny=ny, x_min=x_min, x_max=x_max, y_min=y_min, y_max=y_max, device=device)\n    basis = Basis(polynomial_degree=polynomial_degree, device=device)\n\n    # Create the solver\n    print(\"Initializing solver...\")\n    solver = DGSolver(mesh, basis, initial_conditions_func=initial_conditions_vortex)\n\n\n    output_dir = \"data\"\n    np.savez(\n        os.path.join(output_dir, \"init.npz\"), \n        q=solver.Q.numpy(), \n        x=solver.x.numpy(), \n        y=solver.y.numpy(),\n        vertices=mesh.vertices_host\n    )\n\n    # Run the simulation\n    print(f\"Starting simulation on device '{device}'...\")\n    print(f\"t_final = {t_final}, CFL = {CFL}\")\n    solver.solve(t_final=t_final, CFL=CFL, log_frequency=20)\n    print(\"Simulation finished.\")\n\n    # Save the solution\n    print(\"Saving solution to data/output.npz...\")\n    output_dir = \"data\"\n    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):\n        os.makedirs(output_dir)\n    \n    np.savez(\n        os.path.join(output_dir, \"output.npz\"), \n        q=solver.Q.numpy(), \n        x=solver.x.numpy(), \n        y=solver.y.numpy(),\n        vertices=mesh.vertices_host\n    )\n\n    print(\"Solution saved.\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"2D Discontinuous Galerkin Euler Solver with Nvidia Warp\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--poly_degree\", type=int, default=3, help=\"Polynomial degree for the basis functions.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--nx\", type=int, default=32, help=\"Number of elements in the x-direction.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--ny\", type=int, default=32, help=\"Number of elements in the y-direction.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--t_final\", type=float, default=20.0, help=\"Final simulation time.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--device\", type=str, default=\"cuda\", choices=[\"cuda\", \"cpu\"], help=\"Device to run the simulation on.\")\n    \n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    main(args)\n"
  }
}

Vortex strength\n    r_sq = (x - 5.0)**2 + (y - 5.0)**2\n    \n    u_inf = 1.0\n    v_inf = 1.0\n    \n    du = -(beta / (2 * np.pi)) * np.exp(0.5 * (1 - r_sq)) * (y - 5.0)\n    dv = (beta / (2 * np.pi)) * np.exp(0.5 * (1 - r_sq)) * (x - 5.0)\n    \n    u = u_inf + du\n    v = v_inf + dv\n    \n    T_inf = 1.0\n    T = T_inf - ((gamma - 1) * beta**2 / (8 * gamma * np.pi**2)) * np.exp(1 - r_sq)\n    \n    rho = T**(1.0 / (gamma - 1))\n    p = rho**gamma\n    \n    return rho, u, v, p\n\ndef initial_conditions_uniform(x, y):\n    \"\"\"\n    Uniform flow.\n    \"\"\"\n    rho = 1.0\n    u = 1.0\n    v = 0.0\n    p = 1.0\n    return rho, u, v, p\n\ndef get_initial_condition_func(name):\n    if name == \"vortex\":\n        return initial_conditions_vortex\n    elif name == \"uniform\":\n        return initial_conditions_uniform\n    else:\n        raise ValueError(f\"Unknown initial condition: {name}\")\n\ndef main(config_path):\n    \n    print(f\"Loading configuration from {config_path}...\")\n    with open(config_path, 'r') as f:\n        cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)\n\n    # --- Extract Settings ---\n    sim_cfg = cfg['simulation']\n    mesh_cfg = cfg['mesh']\n    num_cfg = cfg['numerical']\n    ic_cfg = cfg['initial_condition']\n\n    # Simulation parameters\n    polynomial_degree = num_cfg['polynomial_degree']\n    t_final = sim_cfg['t_final']\n    device = sim_cfg.get('device', 'cpu') # Default to CPU for safety\n    CFL = sim_cfg['cfl']\n    log_freq = sim_cfg.get('log_frequency', 10)\n    output_dir = sim_cfg['output_dir']\n\n    # --- Mesh Setup ---\n    print(\"Initializing Mesh...\")\n    if mesh_cfg['type'] == 'cartesian':\n        nx = mesh_cfg['nx']\n        ny = mesh_cfg['ny']\n        x_min = mesh_cfg['x_min']\n        x_max = mesh_cfg['x_max']\n        y_min = mesh_cfg['y_min']\n        y_max = mesh_cfg['y_max']\n        print(f\"  Type: Cartesian ({nx}x{ny})\")\n        mesh = Mesh(nx=nx, ny=ny, x_min=x_min, x_max=x_max, y_min=y_min, y_max=y_max, device=device)\n    \n    elif mesh_cfg['type'] == 'unstructured':\n        filename = mesh_cfg['filename']\n        print(f\"  Type: Unstructured (loading from {filename})\")\n        if not os.path.exists(filename):\n             raise FileNotFoundError(f\"Mesh file not found: {filename}\")\n        mesh = Mesh(filename=filename, device=device)\n    \n    else:\n        raise ValueError(f\"Unknown mesh type: {mesh_cfg['type']}\")\n\n    # --- Basis Setup ---\n    print(f\"Initializing Basis (Poly Degree N={polynomial_degree})...\")\n    basis = Basis(polynomial_degree=polynomial_degree, device=device)\n\n    # --- Solver Setup ---\n    ic_name = ic_cfg['name']\n    print(f\"Initializing Solver with IC: {ic_name}...\")\n    ic_func = get_initial_condition_func(ic_name)\n    solver = DGSolver(mesh, basis, initial_conditions_func=ic_func)\n\n    # --- Output Directory ---\n    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):\n        os.makedirs(output_dir)\n\n    # Save Initial State\n    np.savez(\n        os.path.join(output_dir, \"init.npz\"), \n        q=solver.Q.numpy(), \n        x=solver.x.numpy(), \n        y=solver.y.numpy(),\n        vertices=mesh.vertices_host\n    )\n\n    # --- Run Simulation ---\n    print(f\"Starting simulation on device '{device}'...\")\n    print(f\"t_final = {t_final}, CFL = {CFL}\")\n    \n    solver.solve(t_final=t_final, CFL=CFL, log_frequency=log_freq)\n    \n    print(\"Simulation finished.\")\n\n    # Save Final Solution\n    print(f\"Saving final solution to {output_dir}/output.npz...\")\n    np.savez(\n        os.path.join(output_dir, \"output.npz\"), \n        q=solver.Q.numpy(), \n        x=solver.x.numpy(), \n        y=solver.y.numpy(),\n        vertices=mesh.vertices_host\n    )\n    print(\"Done.\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"2D Discontinuous Galerkin Euler Solver with Nvidia Warp\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"config\", type=str, nargs='?', default=\"config/default.yaml\", help=\"Path to the YAML configuration file.\")\n    \n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    \n    if not os.path.exists(args.config):\n        print(f\"Error: Config file '{args.config}' not found.\")\n        sys.exit(1)\n        \n    main(args.config)"
  }
}

Deine Map-Logik war korrekt für das Flattening row-major (Standard Numpy)\n        # Face 0 (bottom, y=-1), Face 1 (right, x=+1), etc.\n        # Aber Achtung: x changes fast, y changes slow in np.meshgrid('xy')? \n        # Bottom\n        face_nodes[1, :] = np.arange(self.N1-1, self.Np, self.N1) # Right\n        face_nodes[2, :] = np.arange(self.Np - self.N1, self.Np) # Top\n        face_nodes[3, :] = np.arange(0, self.Np - self.N1 + 1, self.N1) # Left\n        return face_nodes\n\n    def _differentiation_matrix_1d(self, nodes):\n        # KORRIGIERT\n        D = np.zeros((self.N1, self.N1))\n        for i in range(self.N1):\n            for j in range(self.N1):\n                if i != j:\n                    Ln_i = legendre(self.N)(nodes[i])\n                    Ln_j = legendre(self.N)(nodes[j])\n                    D[i, j] = Ln_i / (Ln_j * (nodes[i] - nodes[j]))\n                else:\n                    if i == 0:\n                        D[i, j] = -self.N * self.N1 / 4.0\n                    elif i == self.N:\n                        D[i, j] = self.N * self.N1 / 4.0\n                    else:\n                        D[i, j] = 0.0 # WICHTIG: 0 für Legendre!\n        return D\n\n    def _differentiation_matrices_2d(self, D1D):\n        I = np.eye(self.N1)\n        # Achtung: Reihenfolge hängt von deinem Flattening ab.\n        # Wenn nodes_2d via meshgrid/flatten erstellt wurde:\n        # Dr wirkt auf x (fast index) -> Kron(I, D)\n        # Ds wirkt auf y (slow index) -> Kron(D, I)\n        Dr = np.kron(I, D1D) \n        Ds = np.kron(D1D, I)\n        return Dr, Ds\n        \n    def _create_lift_matrix(self, face_nodes, M_face, inv_mass_matrix_diag):\n        \"\"\"\n        LIFT = M^(-1) * E\n        \"\"\"\n        # E Matrix: akkumuliert die Flux-Beiträge\n        E = np.zeros((self.Np, 4 * self.Nfp))\n        \n        for i in range(4):\n            # Indizes der Knoten auf Face i\n            f_idx = face_nodes[i, :]\n            \n            # Da wir Nodal-DG machen, ist die Projektion einfach:\n            # Wir schreiben die 1D Massenmatrix in die entsprechenden Zeilen von E\n            for k in range(self.Nfp):\n                row = f_idx[k]\n                col = i * self.Nfp + k\n                # Diagonaleintrag der Face-Massenmatrix\n                E[row, col] = M_face[k, k] # oder einfach weights_1d[k]\n\n        # Jetzt anwenden von M^(-1). Da M diagonal ist, skalieren wir einfach die Zeilen.\n        # Broadcasting: (Np, 1) * (Np, 4*Nfp)\n        LIFT = inv_mass_matrix_diag[:, None] * E\n        \n        return LIFT\n"

✨ ## MODEL

`basis.py` uses `_gauss_lobatto_quadrature`.
Gauss-Lobatto nodes **include the endpoints** (-1 and 1).
This means the vertices of the quad (corners) ARE present in the DG solution array.
Specifically, for `N` (degree):
*   Bottom-Left: `(-1, -1)` is index 0.
*   Bottom-Right: `(1, -1)` is index `N`.
*   Top-Right: `(1, 1)` is index `Np-1`.
*   Top-Left: `(-1, 1)` is index `Np-1-N`.

This is excellent for visualization!
However, `Mesh.vertices_host` defines the *physical* corners of the element.
My DG nodes are mapped inside.
The physical coordinates of the DG nodes are in `solver.x_host` and `solver.y_host`.

**Strategy for XDMF/HDF5:**
I have `(NumElements, Np)` points in physical space.
I can treat the entire simulation domain as a cloud of `NumElements * Np` points.
BUT ParaView renders volumes better if I define cells.

**Option:**
Define `NumElements` cells.
Each cell is a **High-Order Lagrange Quadrilateral**.
VTK type: `VTK_LAGRANGE_QUADRILATERAL` (Type 70).
ParaView supports arbitrary order Lagrange cells.
The node ordering for `VTK_LAGRANGE_QUADRILATERAL` is:
4 corners first, then edges, then face (internal).
My ordering is `meshgrid` (lexicographical row-major or col-major).
This might require a permutation map.

**Simpler Option (Recommended for now):**
Just output the **Cell Averages** on the standard linear mesh (the `Mesh.vertices`).
This is guaranteed to work with any ParaView version and simple to verify.
The user's requirement is "read hdf5 and unstructured gmsh".
If I just save cell data on the `unstructured gmsh` topology, it works perfectly.

Wait, if I save the solution as Cell Data, I am assigning one value to the *entire element*.
If I want to see the solution distribution *inside* the element, I need to output the `x_host, y_host` points.

**Decision:**
I will implement **Cell Data Average** output first. It's robust and satisfies the "visualize unstructured" requirement.
If the user specifically asks for high-order viz later, I can add it. But for now, "unstructured gmsh" usually implies the linear mesh connectivity.

**Plan:**

2.  Create `src/io/data_writer.py`.
3.  Implement `HDF5Writer`:
    *   File structure:
        *   `/mesh/points`: The vertices of the linear mesh.
        *   `/mesh/cells`: The connectivity of the linear mesh.
        *   `/data/step_N/rho`: Cell-averaged density.
        *   ...
    *   XDMF generator:
        *   Point to `/mesh/points` and `/mesh/cells`.
        *   Define `Attribute` "rho" pointing to `/data/step_N/rho`.
4.  Modify `src/core/solver.py` to use `HDF5Writer`.

```python
import h5py
import numpy as np
import os
from src.physics.equations import conservative_to_primitive

class HDF5Writer:
    def __init__(self, filename, mesh):
        self.filename = filename
        self.mesh = mesh
        self.xmf_filename = filename.replace(".h5", ".xmf")
        self.steps = []
        
        # Initialize HDF5 file and write mesh
        with h5py.File(self.filename, 'w') as f:
            # Create Mesh Group
            mesh_grp = f.create_group("mesh")
            
            # Points: (NumElements * 4, 3)
            # Flatten vertices (NumElems, 4, 2) -> (NumElems*4, 2) -> add z -> (NumElems*4, 3)
            verts_2d = mesh.vertices_host.reshape(-1, 2)
            n_points = verts_2d.shape[0]
            points = np.zeros((n_points, 3), dtype=np.float32)
            points[:, 0] = verts_2d[:, 0]
            points[:, 1] = verts_2d[:, 1]
            
            mesh_grp.create_dataset("points", data=points)
            
            # Connectivity: (NumElements, 4)
            # Just 0,1,2,3 ... because vertices are explicit per element
            conn = np.arange(n_points, dtype=np.int32).reshape(-1, 4)
            mesh_grp.create_dataset("connectivity", data=conn)
            
            # Create Data Group
            f.create_group("data")

    def write_step(self, step, time, Q):
        # Calculate cell averages
        # Q is (NumElements, Np, 4)
        # We want (NumElements, 1) per variable for CellData
        
        # 1. Conservative to Primitive
        # Shape (NumElements, Np, 4) -> (4, NumElements, Np) -> (4, TotalNodes)
        q_reshaped = Q.transpose(2, 0, 1).reshape(4, -1)
        prim = conservative_to_primitive(q_reshaped)
        # -> (4, NumElements, Np)
        prim = prim.reshape(4, Q.shape[0], Q.shape[1])
        
        # 2. Average over Np
        # Shape (4, NumElements)
        avgs = np.mean(prim, axis=2)
        
        rho = avgs[0]
        u   = avgs[1]
        v   = avgs[2]
        p   = avgs[3]
        
        with h5py.File(self.filename, 'a') as f:
            grp = f["data"].create_group(f"step_{step}")
            grp.attrs["time"] = time
            grp.attrs["step"] = step
            
            grp.create_dataset("rho", data=rho)
            grp.create_dataset("u", data=u)
            grp.create_dataset("v", data=v)
            grp.create_dataset("p", data=p)
            
        self.steps.append((step, time))
        self._write_xmf()

    def _write_xmf(self):
        with open(self.xmf_filename, 'w') as f:
            f.write('<?xml version="1.0" ?>\n')
            f.write('<!DOCTYPE Xdmf SYSTEM "Xdmf.dtd" []>\n')
            f.write('<Xdmf Version="3.0">\n')
            f.write(' <Domain>\n')
            f.write('  <Grid Name="TimeSeries" GridType="Collection" CollectionType="Temporal">\n')
            
            h5_rel = os.path.basename(self.filename)
            n_elems = self.mesh.num_elements
            n_points = n_elems * 4
            
            for step, time in self.steps:
                f.write(f'   <Grid Name="Step_{step}" GridType="Uniform">\n')
                f.write(f'    <Time Value="{time}"/>\n')
                
                # Topology
                f.write(f'    <Topology TopologyType="Quadrilateral" NumberOfElements="{n_elems}">\n')
                f.write(f'     <DataItem Dimensions="{n_elems} 4" NumberType="Int" Format="HDF">\n')
                f.write(f'      {h5_rel}:/mesh/connectivity\n')
                f.write(f'     </DataItem>\n')
                f.write(f'    </Topology>\n')
                
                # Geometry
                f.write(f'    <Geometry GeometryType="XYZ">\n')
                f.write(f'     <DataItem Dimensions="{n_points} 3" NumberType="Float" Precision="4" Format="HDF">\n')
                f.write(f'      {h5_rel}:/mesh/points\n')
                f.write(f'     </DataItem>\n')
                f.write(f'    </Geometry>\n')
                
                # Attributes (Cell Data)
                for var in ["rho", "u", "v", "p"]:
                    f.write(f'    <Attribute Name="{var}" AttributeType="Scalar" Center="Cell">\n')
                    f.write(f'     <DataItem Dimensions="{n_elems}" NumberType="Float" Precision="4" Format="HDF">\n')
                    f.write(f'      {h5_rel}:/data/step_{step}/{var}\n')
                    f.write(f'     </DataItem>\n')
                    f.write(f'    </Attribute>\n')
                
                f.write(f'   </Grid>\n')
            
            f.write('  </Grid>\n')
            f.write(' </Domain>\n')
            f.write('</Xdmf>\n')
```

    "output": "import h5py\nimport numpy as np\nimport os\nfrom src.physics.equations import conservative_to_primitive\n\nclass HDF5Writer:\n    def __init__(self, filename, mesh):\n        self.filename = filename\n        self.mesh = mesh\n        self.xmf_filename = filename.replace(\".h5\", \".xmf\")\n        self.steps = []\n        \n        # Ensure output directory exists\n        out_dir = os.path.dirname(filename)\n        if out_dir and not os.path.exists(out_dir):\n            os.makedirs(out_dir)\n        \n        # Initialize HDF5 file and write mesh\n        with h5py.File(self.filename, 'w') as f:\n            # Create Mesh Group\n            mesh_grp = f.create_group(\"mesh\")\n            \n            # Points: (NumElements * 4, 3)\n            # Flatten vertices (NumElems, 4, 2) -> (NumElems*4, 2) -> add z -> (NumElems*4, 3)\n            verts_2d = mesh.vertices_host.reshape(-1, 2)\n            n_points = verts_2d.shape[0]\n            points = np.zeros((n_points, 3), dtype=np.float32)\n            points[:, 0] = verts_2d[:, 0]\n            points[:, 1] = verts_2d[:, 1]\n            \n            mesh_grp.create_dataset(\"points\", data=points)\n            \n            # Connectivity: (NumElements, 4)\n            # Just 0,1,2,3 ... because vertices are explicit per element\n            conn = np.arange(n_points, dtype=np.int32).reshape(-1, 4)\n            mesh_grp.create_dataset(\"connectivity\", data=conn)\n            \n            # Create Data Group\n            f.create_group(\"data\")\n\n    def write_step(self, step, time, Q):\n        # Calculate cell averages\n        # Q is (NumElements, Np, 4)\n        # We want (NumElements, 1) per variable for CellData\n        \n        # 1. Conservative to Primitive\n        # Shape (NumElements, Np, 4) -> (4, NumElements, Np) -> (4, TotalNodes)\n        q_reshaped = Q.transpose(2, 0, 1).reshape(4, -1)\n        prim = conservative_to_primitive(q_reshaped)\n        # -> (4, NumElements, Np)\n        prim = prim.reshape(4, Q.shape[0], Q.shape[1])\n        \n        # 2. Average over Np\n        # Shape (4, NumElements)\n        avgs = np.mean(prim, axis=2)\n        \n        rho = avgs[0]\n        u   = avgs[1]\n        v   = avgs[2]\n        p   = avgs[3]\n        \n        with h5py.File(self.filename, 'a') as f:\n            grp = f[\"data\"].create_group(f\"step_{step}\")\n            grp.attrs[\"time\"] = time\n            grp.attrs[\"step\"] = step\n            \n            grp.create_dataset(\"rho\", data=rho)\n            grp.create_dataset(\"u\", data=u)\n            grp.create_dataset(\"v\", data=v)\n            grp.create_dataset(\"p\", data=p)\n            \n        self.steps.append((step, time))\n        self._write_xmf()\n\n    def _write_xmf(self):\n        with open(self.xmf_filename, 'w') as f:\n            f.write('<?xml version=\"1.0\" ?>\\n')\n            f.write('<!DOCTYPE Xdmf SYSTEM \"Xdmf.dtd\" []>\n')\n            f.write('<Xdmf Version=\"3.0\">\n')\n            f.write(' <Domain>\n')\n            f.write('  <Grid Name=\"TimeSeries\" GridType=\"Collection\" CollectionType=\"Temporal\">\n')\n            \n            h5_rel = os.path.basename(self.filename)\n            n_elems = self.mesh.num_elements\n            n_points = n_elems * 4\n            \n            for step, time in self.steps:\n                f.write(f'   <Grid Name=\"Step_{step}\" GridType=\"Uniform\">\n')\n                f.write(f'    <Time Value=\"{time}\"/>\n')\n                \n                # Topology\n                f.write(f'    <Topology TopologyType=\"Quadrilateral\" NumberOfElements=\"{n_elems}\">\n')\n                f.write(f'     <DataItem Dimensions=\"{n_elems} 4\" NumberType=\"Int\" Format=\"HDF\">\n')\n                f.write(f'      {h5_rel}:/mesh/connectivity\n')\n                f.write(f'     </DataItem>\n')\n                f.write(f'    </Topology>\n')\n                \n                # Geometry\n                f.write(f'    <Geometry GeometryType=\"XYZ\">\n')\n                f.write(f'     <DataItem Dimensions=\"{n_points} 3\" NumberType=\"Float\" Precision=\"4\" Format=\"HDF\">\n')\n                f.write(f'      {h5_rel}:/mesh/points\n')\n                f.write(f'     </DataItem>\n')\n                f.write(f'    </Geometry>\n')\n                \n                # Attributes (Cell Data)\n                for var in [\"rho\", \"u\", \"v\", \"p\"]:\n                    f.write(f'    <Attribute Name=\"{var}\" AttributeType=\"Scalar\" Center=\"Cell\">\n')\n                    f.write(f'     <DataItem Dimensions=\"{n_elems}\" NumberType=\"Float\" Precision=\"4\" Format=\"HDF\">\n')\n                    f.write(f'      {h5_rel}:/data/step_{step}/{var}\n')\n                    f.write(f'     </DataItem>\n')\n                    f.write(f'    </Attribute>\n')\n                \n                f.write(f'   </Grid>\n')\n            \n            f.write('  </Grid>\n')\n            f.write(' </Domain>\n')\n            f.write('</Xdmf>\n')\n"
  }
}

    "content": "import numpy as np\n\ndef vortex(x, y, t=0.0):\n    \"\"\"\n    2D Isentropic Vortex problem.\n    The solution is a vortex that advects diagonally across the domain.\n    Exact solution: q(x, y, t) = q_0(x - u_inf*t, y - v_inf*t)\n    \"\"\"\n    gamma = 1.4\n    beta = 5.0  # Vortex strength\n    \n    u_inf = 1.0\n    v_inf = 1.0\n    \n    # Advect coordinates back to t=0\n    x0 = x - u_inf * t\n    y0 = y - v_inf * t\n    \n    # Center of vortex at t=0\n    xc, yc = 5.0, 5.0\n    \n    r_sq = (x0 - xc)**2 + (y0 - yc)**2\n    \n    du = -(beta / (2 * np.pi)) * np.exp(0.5 * (1 - r_sq)) * (y0 - yc)\n    dv = (beta / (2 * np.pi)) * np.exp(0.5 * (1 - r_sq)) * (x0 - xc)\n    \n    u = u_inf + du\n    v = v_inf + dv\n    \n    T_inf = 1.0\n    T = T_inf - ((gamma - 1) * beta**2 / (8 * gamma * np.pi**2)) * np.exp(1 - r_sq)\n    \n    rho = T**(1.0 / (gamma - 1))\n    p = rho**gamma\n    \n    return rho, u, v, p\n\ndef uniform(x, y, t=0.0):\n    \"\"\"\n    Uniform flow.\n    \"\"\"\n    rho = 1.0\n    u = 1.0\n    v = 0.0\n    p = 1.0\n    return rho, u, v, p\n",

✨ ## MODEL

**4. Generate Mesh**
I will create `tests/verification/vortex_2D/generate_mesh.py` to generate a 20x20 box mesh using `gmsh` python API.
I'll check the syntax for `gmsh` API. I'll stick to a simple quad mesh.

```python
import gmsh
import sys

def generate_mesh(filename):
    gmsh.initialize()
    gmsh.model.add("box")

    # Box [0, 20] x [0, 20]
    lc = 1.0 # Characteristic length
    
    # Points
    p1 = gmsh.model.geo.addPoint(0, 0, 0, lc)
    p2 = gmsh.model.geo.addPoint(20, 0, 0, lc)
    p3 = gmsh.model.geo.addPoint(20, 20, 0, lc)
    p4 = gmsh.model.geo.addPoint(0, 20, 0, lc)

    # Lines
    l1 = gmsh.model.geo.addLine(p1, p2)
    l2 = gmsh.model.geo.addLine(p2, p3)
    l3 = gmsh.model.geo.addLine(p3, p4)
    l4 = gmsh.model.geo.addLine(p4, p1)

    # Curve Loop
    cl = gmsh.model.geo.addCurveLoop([l1, l2, l3, l4])
    
    # Plane Surface
    s = gmsh.model.geo.addPlaneSurface([cl])

    # Transfinite mesh to get perfect quads
    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteCurve(l1, 21) # 20 elements -> 21 nodes
    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteCurve(l2, 21)
    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteCurve(l3, 21)
    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteCurve(l4, 21)
    
    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteSurface(s)
    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setRecombine(2, s) # Recombine triangles into quads

    gmsh.model.geo.synchronize()
    
    gmsh.model.mesh.generate(2)
    
    gmsh.write(filename)
    gmsh.finalize()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    generate_mesh("box.msh")
```

    "content": "import gmsh\nimport sys\nimport os\n\ndef generate_mesh(filename):\n    gmsh.initialize()\n    gmsh.model.add(\"box\")\n\n    # Box [0, 20] x [0, 20]\n    lc = 1.0 # Characteristic length\n    \n    # Points\n    p1 = gmsh.model.geo.addPoint(0, 0, 0, lc)\n    p2 = gmsh.model.geo.addPoint(20, 0, 0, lc)\n    p3 = gmsh.model.geo.addPoint(20, 20, 0, lc)\n    p4 = gmsh.model.geo.addPoint(0, 20, 0, lc)\n\n    # Lines\n    l1 = gmsh.model.geo.addLine(p1, p2)\n    l2 = gmsh.model.geo.addLine(p2, p3)\n    l3 = gmsh.model.geo.addLine(p3, p4)\n    l4 = gmsh.model.geo.addLine(p4, p1)\n\n    # Curve Loop\n    cl = gmsh.model.geo.addCurveLoop([l1, l2, l3, l4])\n    \n    # Plane Surface\n    s = gmsh.model.geo.addPlaneSurface([cl])\n\n    # Transfinite mesh to get perfect quads\n    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteCurve(l1, 21) # 20 elements -> 21 nodes\n    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteCurve(l2, 21)\n    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteCurve(l3, 21)\n    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteCurve(l4, 21)\n    \n    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setTransfiniteSurface(s)\n    gmsh.model.geo.mesh.setRecombine(2, s) # Recombine triangles into quads\n\n    gmsh.model.geo.synchronize()\n    \n    gmsh.model.mesh.generate(2)\n    \n    gmsh.write(filename)\n    gmsh.finalize()\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    # Ensure output directory exists if running standalone\n    out_dir = os.path.dirname(\"box.msh\")\n    if out_dir and not os.path.exists(out_dir):\n        os.makedirs(out_dir)\n    generate_mesh(\"box.msh\")\n",
    "file_path": "tests/verification/vortex_2D/generate_mesh.py"
  }
}

✨ ## MODEL

**6. Create Verification Script**
`tests/verification/vortex_2D/verify.py`.

Logic:
1.  Run simulation.
2.  Load `results.h5`.
3.  Get final step data (rho).
4.  Get mesh points (centroids of cells? No, my output saves cell averages).
5.  Analytical solution at centroids.
6.  Compute error.

Wait, `HDF5Writer` saves `mesh/points` (vertices). It does **not** save cell centers.
To compare cell averages, I need to compute the analytical cell average.
Or simpler: Compute analytical solution at cell **centroid** and compare to numerical cell average. For smooth solutions (Vortex), this is a reasonable approximation for error checking (order 2 accuracy).
Since DG is high order, this degrades the verification order, but for a pass/fail regression test it's fine.

I need to calculate centroids from `mesh/points` and `mesh/connectivity`.
`mesh/points`: `(N_points, 3)`
`mesh/connectivity`: `(N_elems, 4)`

Centroid $x_c = 0.25 * \sum x_i$.

I need `src` in python path.

```python
import sys
import os
import numpy as np
import h5py
import subprocess

# Add project root to path
sys.path.append(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../../..")))

from src.physics.initial_conditions import vortex
from src.physics.equations import conservative_to_primitive

def run_simulation():
    config_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "vortex.yaml")
    # Run from root
    root_dir = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../../.."))
    
    cmd = [sys.executable, "run_simulation.py", config_path]
    print(f"Running: {' '.join(cmd)}")
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=root_dir, capture_output=True, text=True)
    
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print("Simulation failed!")
        print(result.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print("Simulation finished successfully.")

def verify():
    output_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "output")
    h5_file = os.path.join(output_dir, "results.h5")
    
    if not os.path.exists(h5_file):
        print(f"Error: {h5_file} not found.")
        sys.exit(1)
        
    with h5py.File(h5_file, 'r') as f:
        # Load Mesh
        points = f['mesh/points'][:]
        conn = f['mesh/connectivity'][:]
        
        # Calculate Centroids
        # conn is (N_elems, 4)
        # points is (N_points, 3)
        
        # Get coordinates of all 4 nodes for all elements
        # Shape (N_elems, 4, 3)
        element_coords = points[conn] 
        centroids = np.mean(element_coords, axis=1) # (N_elems, 3)
        
        # Load Final Step Data
        # Find last step
        steps = sorted([k for k in f['data'].keys() if k.startswith('step_')])
        last_step = steps[-1]
        print(f"Verifying step: {last_step}")
        
        rho_num = f['data'][last_step]['rho'][:]
        time = f['data'][last_step].attrs['time']
        
        # Calculate Analytical Solution at Centroids
        rho_ana = np.zeros_like(rho_num)
        
        # We need to map centroids (x,y) to analytical function
        # Centroids are in 3D (z=0), we take x,y
        x = centroids[:, 0]
        y = centroids[:, 1]
        
        # Vectorized call to vortex?
        # vortex function is vectorized
        rho_ana, _, _, _ = vortex(x, y, t=time)
        
        # Error (L2 norm relative)
        diff = rho_num - rho_ana
        l2_error = np.linalg.norm(diff) / np.linalg.norm(rho_ana)
        
        print(f"L2 Error (Density): {l2_error:.4e}")
        
        # Threshold
        threshold = 1.0e-2 # 1% error tolerance for this rough check
        if l2_error > threshold:
            print("Test FAILED: Error too high.")
            sys.exit(1)
        else:
            print("Test PASSED.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_simulation()
    verify()
```

**7. Create Global Runner**

```python
import os
import subprocess
import sys

def run_tests():
    root_tests_dir = os.path.dirname(__file__)
    verification_dir = os.path.join(root_tests_dir, "verification")
    
    test_scripts = []
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(verification_dir):
        if "verify.py" in files:
            test_scripts.append(os.path.join(root, "verify.py"))
    
    if not test_scripts:
        print("No tests found.")
        return

    print(f"Found {len(test_scripts)} tests.")
    
    failed_tests = []
    
    for script in test_scripts:
        print(f"\n--- Running {script} ---")
        try:
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, script], check=True)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            failed_tests.append(script)
            print(f"!!! Test {script} FAILED !!!")
    
    print("\n==============================")
    if failed_tests:
        print(f"Tests failed: {len(failed_tests)}")
        for t in failed_tests:
            print(f" - {t}")
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print("All tests PASSED.")
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_tests()
```

**Algorithm:**
1.  Read mesh using `meshio`.
2.  Parse `mesh.cell_sets` or `mesh.cell_data` to find tags. `meshio` behavior with Gmsh 4.1 can be tricky. It often puts tags in `cell_data["gmsh:physical"]`.
3.  Store boundary edges in a dictionary: `edge_to_tag = { (n1, n2): tag }`. (Sort nodes for key).
4.  In the connectivity loop:
    *   If a face is on the boundary (count == 1), look up its edge in `edge_to_tag`.
    *   Store `boundary_flags[element_id, face_idx] = tag`.

class DGSolver:
    def __init__(self, mesh, basis, initial_conditions_func, config=None):
        # ...
        
        # --- Boundary Conditions Setup ---
        # Map (Element, Face) -> BC_TYPE_ID
        # We start with boundary_tags from mesh (Gmsh IDs)
        # We map Gmsh ID -> BC Type ID using config
        
        self.bc_mask_host = np.zeros((mesh.num_elements, 4), dtype=np.int32)
        
        if config and 'boundaries' in config:
            # Constants
            BC_WALL = 1
            BC_FARFIELD = 2
            
            # 1. Build map: GmshTag -> BCTypeID
            tag_to_bc = {}
            for name, bc_conf in config['boundaries'].items():
                # Find tag for this name
                if hasattr(mesh, 'physical_groups') and name in mesh.physical_groups:
                    tag = mesh.physical_groups[name]
                else:
                    # Fallback: maybe user provided tag directly as string?
                    try: 
                        tag = int(name) 
                    except: 
                        print(f"Warning: Boundary '{name}' not found in mesh.")
                        continue
                
                bc_type_str = bc_conf['type']
                if bc_type_str == "slip_wall":
                    tag_to_bc[tag] = BC_WALL
                elif bc_type_str == "farfield" or bc_type_str == "outflow":
                    tag_to_bc[tag] = BC_FARFIELD
                else:
                    print(f"Warning: Unknown BC type '{bc_type_str}'")
            
            # 2. Map mesh.boundary_tags -> bc_mask
            # mesh.boundary_tags_host contains the Gmsh Tags
            for e in range(mesh.num_elements):
                for f in range(4):
                    tag = mesh.boundary_tags_host[e, f]
                    if tag > 0:
                        if tag in tag_to_bc:
                            self.bc_mask_host[e, f] = tag_to_bc[tag]
                        else:
                            # Default to Farfield/Outflow if not specified? 
                            # Or keep 0 (Internal)? 
                            # If it has a tag but no config, it's a boundary without type.
                            # Let's default to Farfield for safety.
                            self.bc_mask_host[e, f] = BC_FARFIELD
        
        self.bc_mask = wp.array(self.bc_mask_host, dtype=wp.int32, device=self.device)

--- Debugging: Directory to save step-by-step results ---\n        # Only used if no writer is provided\n        output_steps_dir = \"data/steps\"\n        if writer is None and not os.path.exists(output_steps_dir):\n            os.makedirs(output_steps_dir)\n        \n        use_stream = self.device == \"cuda\"\n        if use_stream:\n            stream = wp.Stream(device=self.device)\n\n        while t < t_final:\n            \n            # --- Adaptive dt calculation ---\n            self.max_wave_speed.zero_()\n            wp.launch(\n                kernel=wk.compute_max_wave_speed,\n                dim=(self.mesh.num_elements, self.basis.Np),\n                inputs=[self.Q, self.max_wave_speed],\n                device=self.device\n            )\n            max_speed = self.max_wave_speed.numpy()[0]\n            # Smallest distance between any two nodes in the mesh (characteristic length)\n            # A simpler but less robust way is to use dx = mesh.lx / mesh.nx\n            dx = self.mesh.dx \n            dt = CFL * dx / max_speed\n            # print(f\"Calculated dt: {dt:.4e}\")\n\n            # --- End of adaptive dt calculation ---\n\n            if use_stream:\n                with stream:\n                    # Standard SSP-RK3 scheme\n                    self.Q_rk = self.Q\n                    self._compute_rhs()\n                    wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_1, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q_stage1], device=self.device)\n                    \n                    self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage1\n                    self._compute_rhs()\n                    wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_2, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage1, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q_stage2], device=self.device)\n\n                    self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage2\n                    self._compute_rhs()\n                    wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_3, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage2, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q], device=self.device)\n                \n                stream.synchronize()\n            else: # 2nd stage\n                self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage1\n                self._compute_rhs()\n                wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_2, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage1, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q_stage2], device=self.device)\n\n                # 3rd stage\n                self.Q_rk = self.Q_stage2\n                self._compute_rhs()\n                wp.launch(kernel=wk.rk_stage_3, dim=self.Q.shape, inputs=[self.Q, self.Q_stage2, self.rhs, dt], outputs=[self.Q], device=self.device)\n\n                #
